options.B: ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) — routers send Router Advertisement (RA) messages containing the network prefix, prefix length, and default gateway, allowing hosts to autonomously generate their own interface addresses
options.C: ARP broadcasts from the router provide the subnet prefix and gateway MAC address
options.D: DNS AAAA records provide the prefix for autoconfiguration
options.E: This is a requirement of the ISO 27001 standard

questions.explanation: SLAAC relies on ICMPv6 Router Advertisement (RA) messages, which are part of the Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP, RFC 4861). Routers periodically multicast RAs (or send them in response to Router Solicitation messages) containing one or more prefix information options, prefix lengths, valid and preferred lifetimes, and the router's link-local address as the default gateway. The host combines the advertised prefix with a self-generated interface identifier (using EUI-64 or RFC 7217 stable privacy addresses) to form a complete IPv6 address. ARP does not exist in IPv6.

questions.question: What is the IPv6 link-local address prefix, and under what circumstances are link-local addresses used?

options.A: 2001:db8::/32 — used for documentation and testing purposes only
options.B: fe80::/10 — automatically configured on every IPv6-enabled interface and used for communication between nodes on the same network segment, including NDP, routing protocol exchanges, and as next-hop addresses
options.C: fc00::/7 — used for private addressing analogous to RFC 1918 in IPv4
options.D: ff02::/16 — used for multicast communication on the local link
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: IPv6 link-local addresses use the prefix fe80::/10 and are automatically assigned to every IPv6-enabled network interface without any manual configuration or DHCP. They are scoped to the local network segment (link) and are not routable beyond it. Link-local addresses are essential for NDP operations (neighbor solicitation/advertisement, router solicitation/advertisement), routing protocol neighbor adjacencies (OSPFv3, BGP), and serve as default gateway addresses. They are mandatory in IPv6 — a host always has a link-local address even without global connectivity.

questions.question: In IPv6, the Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) replaces several protocols used in IPv4. Which IPv4 protocol is NOT replaced by NDP?

options.A: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) — replaced by NDP Neighbor Solicitation/Advertisement
options.B: ICMP Router Discovery — replaced by NDP Router Solicitation/Advertisement
options.C: DNS (Domain Name System) — which continues to function independently in IPv6 using AAAA records
options.D: DHCP for address autoconfiguration — partially replaced by SLAAC through NDP Router Advertisements
options.E: All of the above

questions.explanation: NDP (RFC 4861) replaces ARP with Neighbor Solicitation/Advertisement messages, replaces ICMP Router Discovery with Router Solicitation/Advertisement, and provides SLAAC as an alternative to DHCP for address configuration. However, DNS remains an independent protocol in IPv6, resolving domain names to AAAA records (128-bit IPv6 addresses) just as it resolves A records for IPv4. NDP also provides Duplicate Address Detection (DAD) and redirect functionality, but DNS resolution is not part of its scope.

questions.question: An IPv6 packet has a 40-byte fixed header. Compared to the IPv4 header, which field was removed from the IPv6 header to simplify router processing?

options.A: Source Address and Destination Address fields
options.B: The Header Checksum field — routers no longer recalculate a checksum at each hop, and integrity checking is delegated to Layer 2 (Ethernet CRC) and Layer 4 (TCP/UDP checksums)
options.C: The Hop Limit field (equivalent to IPv4 TTL)
options.D: The Next Header field (equivalent to IPv4 Protocol field)
options.E: Only after formal approval from the board of directors

questions.explanation: IPv6 eliminated the Header Checksum field that existed in IPv4. In IPv4, routers must recalculate the header checksum at every hop because the TTL field changes, adding processing overhead. IPv6 removes this requirement, relying instead on Layer 2 error detection (e.g., Ethernet FCS/CRC-32) and upper-layer checksums (TCP, UDP, ICMPv6 all include pseudo-header checksums that cover source and destination addresses). This design decision significantly improves router forwarding performance.

questions.question: An organisation is running a dual-stack network during their IPv4 to IPv6 transition. A penetration tester discovers that IPv6 is enabled on all hosts but the network security controls (firewall rules, IDS signatures) only cover IPv4 traffic. Which attack is most feasible in this scenario?

options.A: Exploiting IPv6 fragmentation to bypass the IPv4 firewall and reach filtered services
options.B: Setting up a rogue IPv6 router (sending Router Advertisements) to become the default gateway via SLAAC, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks on IPv6 traffic that bypasses IPv4-only security controls
options.C: Using Teredo tunnelling to encapsulate IPv4 attacks within IPv6 headers
options.D: Performing DNS rebinding attacks that only work over IPv6
options.E: This is not a requirement for CREST certification

questions.explanation: On dual-stack networks where IPv6 security controls are not implemented, an attacker can send forged Router Advertisement messages to become the network's IPv6 default gateway. Hosts using SLAAC will accept these RAs and route IPv6 traffic through the attacker. Since many modern operating systems prefer IPv6 over IPv4 (per RFC 6724), DNS queries that return both A and AAAA records will cause hosts to connect via IPv6 through the attacker, completely bypassing IPv4 firewalls and IDS. This is commonly performed using tools like mitm6 or THC-IPv6.

questions.question: A penetration tester sends a UDP datagram to a closed port on a target host and receives an ICMP Destination Unreachable (Port Unreachable) message. However, when scanning many UDP ports, some ports show as 'open|filtered' in nmap. Why does this ambiguity occur?

options.A: UDP services always respond to probes, so open|filtered indicates a firewall is modifying the response
options.B: Open UDP ports typically send no response to an arbitrary probe (the service may silently discard packets it does not understand), making it impossible to distinguish between an open port that silently dropped the packet and a firewall filtering the port by dropping the packet
options.C: Nmap cannot determine UDP port states and always reports open|filtered
options.D: The target's TCP/IP stack is rate-limiting ICMP responses, causing false positives on all ports
options.E: It depends on the specific country's jurisdiction

questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless, so there is no SYN/SYN-ACK/RST handshake to definitively determine port state. When a UDP probe receives no response, nmap cannot distinguish between an open port (where the service silently discarded the unexpected probe) and a filtered port (where a firewall dropped the packet). Only a closed port generates a definitive ICMP Port Unreachable response. Using service-specific probes (nmap -sUV or --version-intensity) can help, as legitimate services respond to properly formatted requests, reducing open|filtered ambiguity.

questions.question: A penetration tester runs nmap with the -sV flag and discovers that port 8443 returns a banner identifying itself as 'Apache httpd 2.4.49'. However, the tester suspects the banner may have been modified. Which additional technique best verifies the actual service and version?

options.A: Trust the banner as services cannot modify their version strings
options.B: Analyse the service's behaviour by examining TLS certificate details, HTTP response headers (Server, X-Powered-By), HTML content patterns, and protocol-specific probes; compare nmap's probe response signatures against its nmap-service-probes database for behavioural fingerprinting beyond banner text
options.C: Perform a SYN scan on the same port to determine the actual service version
options.D: Use the -O flag to perform OS detection, which will also correct service version inaccuracies
options.E: Only when using automated scanning tools

questions.explanation: Banners can be easily modified or spoofed as a defensive measure. Nmap's version detection (-sV) goes beyond banner grabbing by sending protocol-specific probes and analysing responses against its nmap-service-probes signature database. Additional verification includes: examining TLS certificates for organisation and hostname details, analysing HTTP headers for technology fingerprints, checking default error pages and favicon hashes, and using tools like WhatWeb or Wappalyzer. Behavioural fingerprinting is significantly harder to fake than modifying a banner string.

questions.question: A penetration tester is performing host discovery on an internal network where ICMP echo requests are blocked by host-based firewalls on most machines. Which nmap host discovery technique is most likely to identify live hosts in this environment?

options.B: nmap -sn -PS22,80,443,445 -PA80,443 — combining TCP SYN and TCP ACK probes to common ports, as host-based firewalls that block ICMP often still permit responses to TCP probes on open service ports
options.E: This is handled by the client's internal IT department

questions.explanation: When ICMP is blocked, TCP-based discovery probes are more effective. TCP SYN probes (-PS) to common ports elicit SYN/ACK (open) or RST (closed) responses, and TCP ACK probes (-PA) elicit RST responses from live hosts. Combining multiple probe types and targeting common service ports (SSH, HTTP, HTTPS, SMB) maximises the chance of receiving a response. On internal networks, port 445 (SMB) is particularly effective for discovering Windows hosts. Using multiple discovery techniques simultaneously provides the most comprehensive results.

questions.question: A penetration tester discovers that a target telecom system uses SCTP (Stream Control Transmission Protocol) on several ports. Which characteristic of SCTP's connection establishment process makes it more resistant to SYN flood attacks compared to TCP?

options.A: SCTP does not use any form of handshake, making connection flooding impossible
options.B: SCTP uses a four-way handshake (INIT, INIT-ACK, COOKIE-ECHO, COOKIE-ACK) where the server does not allocate resources until the client returns a valid cookie in the COOKIE-ECHO chunk, preventing state exhaustion from spoofed source addresses
options.C: SCTP encrypts all connection establishment packets, making it impossible to spoof source addresses
options.D: SCTP uses UDP as its transport layer, inheriting UDP's connectionless resistance to SYN floods
options.E: During the post-engagement debrief session

questions.explanation: SCTP's four-way handshake includes a cookie mechanism that protects against resource exhaustion attacks analogous to TCP SYN floods. When a client sends INIT, the server responds with INIT-ACK containing a state cookie (a cryptographic token encoding connection parameters) but does NOT allocate any Transmission Control Block (TCB) resources. Only when the client echoes the valid cookie back in COOKIE-ECHO does the server create state and respond with COOKIE-ACK. This means an attacker cannot exhaust server memory by sending INITs with spoofed source addresses, as the server holds no per-connection state until the handshake completes. SCTP is commonly found on telecom infrastructure using protocols like SIGTRAN, Diameter, and SS7-over-IP.

questions.question: Which built-in Windows command provides detailed system information including OS version, hotfixes installed, and network configuration during initial reconnaissance?

options.B: systeminfo
options.E: Only if the vulnerability is classified as Critical

questions.explanation: The 'systeminfo' command provides comprehensive system details including OS name/version, registered owner, system manufacturer, processor information, installed hotfixes, and network card configurations — making it the most complete single reconnaissance command.

questions.question: Which BloodHound edge represents the ability to perform a DCSync attack to replicate directory data including password hashes?

options.B: GetChanges and GetChangesAll
options.E: This is a standard feature of most antivirus software

questions.explanation: DCSync requires both DS-Replication-Get-Changes and DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All extended rights. In BloodHound, these are represented as GetChanges and GetChangesAll edges, which together allow replication of password data from a domain controller.

questions.question: What is the primary risk of the WDigest authentication protocol on older Windows systems, and how can it be exploited post-compromise?

options.A: WDigest stores passwords in reversible encryption in the SAM file
options.B: WDigest caches plaintext credentials in LSASS memory, extractable with tools like mimikatz
options.C: WDigest transmits passwords in cleartext over the network
options.D: WDigest disables account lockout policies allowing brute force
options.E: Only during the initial scoping meeting

questions.explanation: WDigest authentication (enabled by default on Windows 7/2008R2 and earlier) stores plaintext credentials in LSASS process memory. Post-compromise, attackers can extract these using mimikatz's 'sekurlsa::wdigest' command. Microsoft addressed this with KB2871997 allowing WDigest to be disabled via registry.

questions.question: During a penetration test, which technique involves injecting malicious code into a suspended process by unmapping its legitimate code and replacing it with shellcode?

options.B: Process hollowing (RunPE)
options.E: This is not applicable to web application testing

questions.explanation: Process hollowing (also called RunPE) creates a process in a suspended state, unmaps its legitimate executable image using NtUnmapViewOfSection, writes malicious code to the process memory, then resumes execution. This makes the malicious code appear to run under a legitimate process name.

questions.question: Which Windows command-line tool can display and modify discretionary access control lists (DACLs) on files and directories?

options.B: icacls
options.E: Only if requested by the third-party hosting provider

questions.explanation: icacls (Integrity Control Access Control Lists) is the modern Windows tool for viewing and modifying DACLs. It replaced the older cacls command and supports features like inheritance, integrity levels, and saving/restoring ACLs. It can grant, deny, and remove permissions on files and directories.

questions.question: Which vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2020-1472 (Zerologon), allows an unauthenticated attacker to gain domain admin privileges?

options.A: A buffer overflow in the SMB protocol handler
options.B: A cryptographic flaw in the Netlogon protocol (MS-NRPC) allowing authentication bypass
options.C: An RCE vulnerability in the Print Spooler service
options.D: A privilege escalation via Windows Task Scheduler
options.E: This is a requirement of the GDPR only

questions.explanation: Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) exploits a flaw in the Netlogon Remote Protocol's (MS-NRPC) use of AES-CFB8 encryption. By sending Netlogon messages with all-zero client credentials, an attacker can set the domain controller's machine account password to empty, gaining full domain admin access without authentication.

questions.question: Which Windows privilege, when assigned to a service account, allows an attacker to impersonate any user's token for privilege escalation?

options.B: SeImpersonatePrivilege
options.E: Only when performing a white-box test

questions.explanation: SeImpersonatePrivilege allows a process to impersonate a client's security token. Tools like JuicyPotato, PrintSpoofer, and GodPotato exploit this privilege (commonly assigned to service accounts and IIS application pools) to escalate from service account to SYSTEM by coercing a SYSTEM-level process to authenticate.

questions.question: Which technique exploits a vulnerable kernel-mode driver to read and write arbitrary kernel memory for privilege escalation?

options.B: Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD)
options.E: This is handled by the ISP

questions.explanation: BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) involves loading a legitimately signed but vulnerable kernel driver onto the target system. The attacker then exploits the driver's vulnerabilities (such as arbitrary read/write primitives) to modify kernel structures like process tokens, escalating privileges to SYSTEM.

questions.question: Which Windows persistence mechanism survives reboots by storing a DLL path in the registry key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\AppInit_DLLs?

options.B: AppInit DLL persistence
options.E: Only if the tester has a valid security clearance

questions.explanation: AppInit_DLLs is a registry value that causes the listed DLLs to be loaded into every process that loads user32.dll. While modern Windows versions require the DLLs to be code-signed (and the feature can be disabled via Secure Boot), it remains a viable persistence vector on older or misconfigured systems.

questions.question: Which tool can a penetration tester use to identify missing Windows patches by comparing installed hotfixes against known vulnerabilities?

options.B: ProcMon
options.E: This is not a standard part of the penetration testing lifecycle

questions.explanation: Sherlock (and its successor Watson) are PowerShell scripts that check which patches are installed on a Windows system and compare them against a database of known privilege escalation vulnerabilities, identifying missing patches that could be exploited for local privilege escalation.

questions.question: Which attack against Microsoft Exchange Server allows an attacker to impersonate any user by exploiting the EWS (Exchange Web Services) SSRF vulnerability known as ProxyLogon?

options.A: Exploiting OWA login form for credential harvesting
options.B: Chaining CVE-2021-26855 (SSRF) with CVE-2021-27065 (arbitrary file write) for unauthenticated RCE
options.E: Only after the final report has been delivered

questions.explanation: ProxyLogon chains CVE-2021-26855 (a pre-auth SSRF in Exchange's server-side request handlers) with CVE-2021-27065 (an arbitrary file write via Exchange Unified Messaging). Together, these allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands as SYSTEM on the Exchange server.

questions.question: During a network assessment, you capture traffic on port 23 and observe plaintext credentials being transmitted. Which protocol is in use and what is the recommended secure alternative?

options.B: Telnet; replace with SSH
options.C: SNMP v1; replace with SNMP v3
options.E: This is a requirement of the ISO 27001 standard

questions.explanation: Port 23 is the default port for Telnet, which transmits all data including credentials in cleartext. SSH (port 22) provides encrypted communication and should always be used instead of Telnet for remote administration.

questions.question: Which protocol provides out-of-band hardware management capabilities including remote console access, power control, and sensor monitoring, but is frequently misconfigured with default credentials?

options.B: IPMI (Intelligent Platform Management Interface)
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: IPMI provides out-of-band management via a Baseboard Management Controller (BMC), allowing remote power cycling, console access, and hardware monitoring even when the OS is unresponsive. IPMI implementations (Dell iDRAC, HP iLO, Supermicro) are frequently found with default credentials and known vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which vulnerability in RDP's Network Level Authentication (NLA) implementation could allow an attacker to perform a man-in-the-middle attack if the target's certificate is not properly validated?

options.B: Self-signed certificate acceptance without verification
options.E: All of the above

questions.explanation: CVE-2018-0886 is a vulnerability in the Credential Security Support Provider (CredSSP) used by RDP's NLA. An attacker in a MITM position could exploit this to relay credentials and execute code on the target server, as CredSSP did not properly validate the server's identity during the authentication handshake.

questions.question: During an IPsec VPN assessment, which IKE aggressive mode vulnerability allows an attacker to capture the pre-shared key hash for offline cracking?

options.A: The responder sends its identity and hash in cleartext in the first reply
options.B: IKE uses DES encryption by default
options.C: The Diffie-Hellman exchange is performed without authentication
options.D: Phase 2 Quick Mode transmits session keys unencrypted
options.E: Only after formal approval from the board of directors

questions.explanation: In IKE aggressive mode, the responder sends its identity and a hash of the pre-shared key in the first response message (unencrypted). An attacker can capture this hash using tools like ike-scan and crack it offline with tools like psk-crack or hashcat, recovering the VPN pre-shared key.

questions.question: Which file on a Unix system, when misconfigured, allows remote users to execute commands via rsh without password authentication?

options.B: ~/.rhosts or /etc/hosts.equiv
options.E: This is not a requirement for CREST certification

questions.explanation: The ~/.rhosts file (per-user) and /etc/hosts.equiv (system-wide) define trusted host/user combinations for Berkeley r-commands (rsh, rlogin, rexec). Entries like '+ +' grant access from any host as any user, allowing unauthenticated remote command execution.

questions.question: What is the security risk of running 'xhost +' on an X11 server, and how can an attacker exploit it?

options.A: It enables X11 forwarding over SSH, exposing the session to MITM
options.B: It disables access controls, allowing any host to connect and capture keystrokes or screenshots
options.C: It opens a reverse shell via the X11 display manager
options.D: It shares the clipboard contents over the network
options.E: It depends on the specific country's jurisdiction

questions.explanation: 'xhost +' disables all X11 access controls, allowing any remote host to connect to the X display server. An attacker can then use tools like xspy to capture keystrokes, xwd to take screenshots, or inject keystrokes into the victim's session using xdotool.

questions.question: Which information can an attacker enumerate using the finger service (port 79) against a Unix system?

options.B: Usernames, login times, idle times, and home directories
options.E: Only when using automated scanning tools

questions.explanation: The finger service provides user information including usernames, real names, login/idle times, terminal names, home directories, and shell paths. Queries like 'finger @target' enumerate all logged-in users, while 'finger user@target' provides detailed information about a specific user.

questions.question: Which command queries the RPC portmapper on a target to enumerate registered RPC services and their associated ports?

options.B: rpcinfo -p target
options.E: This is handled by the client's internal IT department

questions.explanation: rpcinfo -p queries the portmapper (rpcbind) service on port 111 to list all registered RPC programs, their versions, protocols (TCP/UDP), and port numbers. This reveals services like NFS, NIS/YP, mountd, and statd that may be exploitable.

questions.question: Which NTP command can be abused for reconnaissance and DDoS amplification attacks by returning a list of the last 600 clients that contacted the NTP server?

options.B: monlist (MON_GETLIST_1)
options.E: During the post-engagement debrief session

questions.explanation: The monlist command (MON_GETLIST_1) returns the list of up to 600 hosts that have recently communicated with the NTP server. This provides reconnaissance data and can be abused for DDoS amplification, as a small request generates a large response (amplification factor up to 556x).

questions.question: Which IPMI vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to retrieve password hashes for any valid user account via the RAKP protocol?

options.B: IPMI 2.0 RAKP authentication hash disclosure
options.C: IPMI SOL (Serial over LAN) buffer overflow
options.E: Only if the vulnerability is classified as Critical

questions.explanation: IPMI 2.0's RAKP (Remote Authenticated Key-Exchange Protocol) authentication process discloses the salted SHA1 or MD5 hash of any valid username during the key exchange. An unauthenticated attacker can retrieve these hashes and crack them offline. This is a design flaw in the protocol specification, not an implementation bug.

questions.question: During a penetration test, you discover a service running a version known to have a publicly available exploit. What is the MOST appropriate next step?

options.A: Immediately execute the public exploit in production
options.B: Verify the vulnerability with a safe detection method, assess impact, and exploit only within agreed scope
options.C: Report the finding without any verification
options.D: Scan the entire network for the same vulnerability before reporting
options.E: This is a standard feature of most antivirus software

questions.explanation: Professional practice requires verifying the vulnerability exists (using version checks, safe probes, or non-destructive PoCs) before exploitation. Impact assessment and scope verification ensure testing stays within agreed boundaries and avoids unintended disruption to production services.

questions.question: Which technique allows an attacker to defeat a tamper-evident seal on a device enclosure without leaving visible evidence of intrusion?

options.A: Applying heat or solvents to carefully remove and reapply the seal
options.B: Cutting through the device chassis with a rotary tool
options.C: Replacing the entire enclosure with a new one
options.D: Using an electromagnetic pulse to disable the seal's sensor
options.E: Only during the initial scoping meeting

questions.explanation: Many tamper-evident seals (adhesive labels, shrink wraps, and some holographic seals) can be defeated by applying heat, solvents, or careful mechanical techniques to remove and reapply them without visible evidence. This is why high-security environments use multiple types of seals and regular physical inspection schedules.

questions.question: How can an attacker with physical access exploit PXE (Preboot Execution Environment) boot to compromise a system?

options.A: By modifying the BIOS firmware directly
options.B: By setting up a rogue DHCP/TFTP server to serve a malicious boot image
options.C: By injecting code into the CPU microcode
options.D: By replacing the hard drive with a pre-configured one
options.E: This is not applicable to web application testing

questions.explanation: PXE boot relies on DHCP for IP configuration and TFTP for downloading boot images. An attacker on the local network can set up a rogue DHCP server that responds to PXE requests with a malicious TFTP server address, serving a compromised boot image that provides full system access.

questions.question: Which UEFI Secure Boot bypass technique involves loading a legitimately signed but vulnerable bootloader that can then load unsigned code?

options.B: Using a signed shim with a known vulnerability (e.g., BootHole)
options.D: Flashing a modified UEFI firmware via SPI
options.E: Only if requested by the third-party hosting provider

questions.explanation: The BootHole vulnerability (CVE-2020-10713) in the GRUB2 bootloader allowed arbitrary code execution despite Secure Boot. Since GRUB2 was legitimately signed by Microsoft's third-party UEFI CA, the signed but vulnerable bootloader could bypass Secure Boot protections to load unsigned or malicious code.

questions.question: Which attack can recover BitLocker encryption keys from a system that uses TPM-only authentication without a PIN or startup key?

options.B: Sniffing the TPM-to-CPU communication bus (SPI or LPC) during boot to capture the Volume Master Key
options.C: Exploiting a vulnerability in the AES algorithm
options.D: Extracting the key from the Windows registry while the system is off
options.E: This is a requirement of the GDPR only

questions.explanation: When BitLocker uses TPM-only authentication, the Volume Master Key (VMK) is automatically released by the TPM during boot. An attacker with physical access can use a logic analyzer or FPGA to sniff the SPI or LPC bus between the TPM chip and CPU, capturing the VMK as it's transmitted in cleartext.

questions.question: What is a cold boot attack and how does it threaten full-disk encryption?

options.A: Booting from a USB device to bypass the OS login screen
options.B: Cooling RAM to slow data decay, then extracting encryption keys from memory after a reboot
options.C: Exploiting the bootloader to skip the encryption password prompt
options.D: Brute-forcing the disk encryption password via a GPU cluster
options.E: Only when performing a white-box test

questions.explanation: A cold boot attack exploits the fact that DRAM retains data for seconds to minutes after power loss, especially when cooled. By cooling the RAM modules (e.g., with compressed air), removing them or rebooting into a minimal OS, an attacker can dump memory contents and extract full-disk encryption keys that were stored in RAM.

questions.question: How can an attacker exploit Windows Safe Mode to bypass security controls during a physical security assessment?

options.A: Safe Mode enables remote desktop by default
options.B: Safe Mode loads minimal drivers and services, often bypassing endpoint protection, antivirus, and Group Policy restrictions
options.C: Safe Mode disables all user authentication
options.D: Safe Mode provides direct access to encrypted volumes without passwords
options.E: This is handled by the ISP

questions.explanation: Windows Safe Mode loads only essential drivers and services, which means many security tools (antivirus, EDR agents, DLP solutions) and Group Policy restrictions may not be active. An attacker with physical access can boot into Safe Mode to bypass these protections and perform malicious actions.

questions.question: At which phase of the Secure Development Lifecycle (SDLC) should threat modelling be performed?

options.B: During the design phase, before implementation begins
options.D: Only when a security incident occurs
options.E: Only if the tester has a valid security clearance

questions.explanation: Threat modelling should be performed during the design phase of the SDLC, before code is written. This allows security requirements to be identified early, architectural flaws to be addressed before implementation, and security controls to be designed into the system from the start.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'security gate' in a CI/CD pipeline?

options.A: To encrypt all source code before deployment
options.B: To automatically block builds or deployments that fail security checks (SAST, DAST, dependency scanning)
options.C: To restrict developer access to the repository
options.D: To generate security documentation for compliance
options.E: This is not a standard part of the penetration testing lifecycle

questions.explanation: Security gates are automated checkpoints in CI/CD pipelines that evaluate security scan results (SAST, DAST, SCA, container scanning) against defined policies. Builds or deployments that exceed acceptable risk thresholds (e.g., critical vulnerabilities found) are automatically blocked until remediated.

questions.question: What is the 'shift-left' approach in DevSecOps?

options.A: Moving security testing to occur earlier in the development lifecycle rather than only at the end
options.B: Shifting security responsibilities from developers to a dedicated security team
options.C: Moving production workloads to the left-most availability zone
options.D: Reducing the number of security tools used in the pipeline
options.E: Only after the final report has been delivered

questions.explanation: Shift-left means integrating security activities earlier in the development lifecycle — during design, coding, and build phases rather than only during testing or post-deployment. This catches vulnerabilities sooner when they're cheaper and easier to fix, and builds security awareness among developers.

questions.question: Which type of security testing tool analyses source code without executing it to identify potential vulnerabilities?

options.B: SAST (Static Application Security Testing)
options.E: This is a requirement of the ISO 27001 standard

questions.explanation: SAST tools analyse source code, bytecode, or binary code without executing the application. They identify vulnerabilities such as SQL injection, XSS, buffer overflows, and insecure cryptographic usage by examining code patterns and data flows. SAST can be integrated early in development as it doesn't require a running application.

questions.question: What is Software Composition Analysis (SCA) and why is it important in the development lifecycle?

options.A: It analyses the runtime behaviour of applications in production
options.B: It identifies open-source and third-party components in the codebase and checks them against known vulnerability databases
options.C: It performs load testing to identify performance bottlenecks
options.D: It encrypts source code to prevent intellectual property theft
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: SCA tools inventory all open-source and third-party dependencies in a project and cross-reference them against vulnerability databases (CVE, NVD, OSV). This is critical because modern applications often consist of 80-90% third-party code, and vulnerable dependencies (like Log4Shell) can introduce severe security risks.

questions.question: Why is it essential for a penetration tester to maintain a detailed activity log with timestamps throughout an engagement?

options.A: To increase the billable hours for the engagement
options.B: To provide an audit trail that can distinguish tester activity from real attacks and support the reproducibility of findings
options.C: To satisfy marketing requirements for case studies
options.D: To automatically generate the final report
options.E: All of the above

questions.explanation: Detailed timestamped logs serve multiple purposes: they allow SOC teams to distinguish tester activity from genuine threats, support the reproducibility and verification of findings, provide evidence in case of disputes, and demonstrate due diligence and professionalism in the engagement.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an executive summary in a penetration test report?

options.A: To list every technical vulnerability with exploitation steps
options.B: To provide a high-level overview of findings, risk posture, and strategic recommendations for non-technical stakeholders
options.C: To document the tools and methodologies used during testing
options.D: To include raw output from scanning tools
options.E: Only after formal approval from the board of directors

questions.explanation: The executive summary is written for non-technical stakeholders (C-suite, board members, managers) and should communicate the overall risk posture, key findings, business impact, and strategic recommendations in plain language without technical jargon.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct order of sections in a standard penetration test report?

options.A: Technical Findings → Executive Summary → Methodology → Appendices
options.B: Executive Summary → Scope and Methodology → Findings (prioritised by risk) → Remediation Recommendations → Appendices
options.C: Tool Output → Screenshots → Vulnerability List → Conclusion
options.D: Cover Page → Findings → Executive Summary → Scope
options.E: This is not a requirement for CREST certification

questions.explanation: A professional penetration test report follows a structured format: Executive Summary (for non-technical readers), Scope and Methodology (what was tested and how), Findings prioritised by risk severity, detailed Remediation Recommendations, and Appendices (raw data, tool output, supplementary evidence).

questions.question: When writing a finding in a penetration test report, which elements should be included for each vulnerability?

options.A: Only the CVE number and a generic description
options.B: Title, risk rating, description, evidence/proof, affected assets, impact statement, and remediation guidance
options.C: Only a screenshot proving the vulnerability exists
options.D: The Metasploit module name and raw terminal output
options.E: It depends on the specific country's jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Each finding should include a descriptive title, risk/severity rating (e.g., CVSS score), clear description of the vulnerability, evidence/proof of concept, list of affected assets, business impact statement, and actionable remediation guidance. This structure helps both technical teams and management understand and act on the finding.

questions.question: What risk rating system is most commonly used in penetration testing reports to provide a standardised severity score for each vulnerability?

options.B: CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System)
options.D: Both B and C are commonly used
options.E: Only when using automated scanning tools

questions.explanation: Both CVSS and the OWASP Risk Rating Methodology are commonly used in penetration test reports. CVSS provides a standardised numerical score (0-10) based on attack characteristics, while OWASP considers both likelihood and impact in a contextual risk matrix. Many reports use CVSS for individual vulnerabilities and OWASP-style ratings for business context.

questions.question: Why should a penetration test report include remediation recommendations with prioritisation?

options.A: To demonstrate the tester's expertise in system administration
options.B: To give the client actionable steps to fix vulnerabilities, ordered by risk severity, enabling efficient allocation of remediation resources
options.C: To increase the length of the report for billing purposes
options.D: To replace the need for a follow-up retest
options.E: This is handled by the client's internal IT department

questions.explanation: Prioritised remediation guidance helps clients understand which vulnerabilities pose the greatest risk and should be fixed first. This enables efficient resource allocation, supports risk-based decision making, and provides development/operations teams with clear, actionable steps to improve the organisation's security posture.

questions.question: Before starting a penetration test, what is the MOST important consideration when preparing the testing platform and toolkit?

options.A: Using the newest untested tools for better results
options.B: Ensuring all tools are up to date, licensed appropriately, and the platform is hardened to protect client data
options.C: Installing as many tools as possible for maximum coverage
options.D: Using the client's own infrastructure as the testing platform
options.E: During the post-engagement debrief session

questions.explanation: Platform preparation requires updated tools with current signatures/databases, appropriate licensing (especially for commercial tools), and a hardened testing platform that protects collected client data. The platform should use full-disk encryption, secure communications, and proper data handling procedures.

questions.question: How does an ORM injection attack differ from a traditional SQL injection?

options.A: ORM injection targets the query language or API of the ORM framework (e.g., HQL, Criteria API) rather than raw SQL
options.B: ORM injection can only be performed against NoSQL databases
options.C: ORM injection is a client-side attack that modifies JavaScript
options.D: ORM injection attacks are impossible because ORMs inherently prevent all injection
options.E: Only if the vulnerability is classified as Critical

questions.explanation: ORM injection targets the abstraction layer's query language rather than raw SQL. For example, Hibernate Query Language (HQL) injection involves manipulating HQL queries, which the ORM then translates to SQL. While ORMs reduce SQL injection risk through parameterisation, they don't eliminate injection if developers concatenate user input into ORM queries.

questions.question: Which payload could be used to bypass an LDAP authentication filter that constructs queries like '(&(uid=USER)(userPassword=PASS))'?

options.B: admin)(&))(|(uid=*
options.E: This is a standard feature of most antivirus software

questions.explanation: Injecting 'admin)(|(password=*))' into the uid field modifies the LDAP filter to '(&(uid=admin)(|(password=*))(userPassword=PASS))'. The OR condition (|(password=*)) matches any password value, effectively bypassing the authentication check. LDAP injection uses parentheses and filter operators rather than SQL syntax.

questions.question: In an email header injection attack, which character sequence allows an attacker to add additional email headers such as BCC recipients?

options.B: CRLF characters (\r\n) followed by additional header fields like 'Bcc: attacker@evil.com'
options.C: HTML <script> tags in the subject line
options.D: URL-encoded semicolons in the message body
options.E: Only during the initial scoping meeting

questions.explanation: Email headers are separated by CRLF (\r\n) sequences. By injecting \r\nBcc: attacker@evil.com into a header field (e.g., From, Subject), an attacker can add arbitrary headers including Bcc recipients, effectively using the application's mail server to send spam or exfiltrate data.

questions.question: What is HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP) and how can it be used to bypass security controls?

options.A: Encrypting HTTP parameters to hide malicious payloads
options.B: Submitting the same parameter multiple times with different values, exploiting differences in how frontend and backend servers handle duplicate parameters
options.C: Modifying the HTTP version number in the request
options.D: Changing the Content-Type header to bypass WAF rules
options.E: This is not applicable to web application testing

questions.explanation: HPP exploits the fact that different web technologies handle duplicate HTTP parameters differently — some take the first value, some the last, and some concatenate them. An attacker can bypass WAFs or input validation by splitting malicious input across duplicate parameters that are processed differently by the WAF and the application.

questions.question: During a kiosk breakout assessment, which technique uses the 'Save As' or 'Open' file dialogs in an application to navigate the filesystem and launch cmd.exe?

options.B: Typing a UNC path or file:// URI in the file dialog's address bar to access the filesystem and execute programs
options.C: Exploiting a buffer overflow in the kiosk application
options.D: Using remote desktop to connect to another machine
options.E: Only if requested by the third-party hosting provider

questions.explanation: File dialogs (Save As, Open, Print) often provide filesystem access that kiosk lockdown solutions fail to restrict. By typing paths like 'C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe' in the filename field or navigating via the dialog's address bar, an attacker can browse the filesystem and execute arbitrary programs to escape the kiosk environment.

questions.question: Which Windows accessibility feature can be exploited during a kiosk breakout to launch a command prompt before user login?

options.B: Sticky Keys (sethc.exe) replaced with cmd.exe
options.E: This is a requirement of the GDPR only

questions.explanation: Replacing sethc.exe (Sticky Keys) or utilman.exe (Utility Manager) with cmd.exe allows an attacker to press Shift 5 times or Win+U at the login screen to spawn a SYSTEM-level command prompt. This is a classic kiosk/lockdown bypass technique when the attacker has physical access or can modify files.

questions.question: In a locked-down Windows environment, how can an attacker use Internet Explorer or Edge to escape the browser-based kiosk?

options.A: By exploiting a zero-day browser vulnerability
options.B: By using the browser's developer tools (F12) or JavaScript console to access the filesystem via ActiveX or file:// protocol
options.C: By performing a SQL injection on the kiosk web application
options.D: By connecting to a Wi-Fi network to bypass restrictions
options.E: Only when performing a white-box test

questions.explanation: Browser-based kiosks can often be escaped using developer tools (F12), JavaScript console commands, the file:// protocol, or help menus that link to local files. Internet Explorer's ActiveX support and Edge's DevTools can provide filesystem access and the ability to launch external applications.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut or technique can bypass a kiosk-mode application that replaces the default Windows shell?

options.A: Ctrl+Alt+Del to access Task Manager, then launching a new process
options.B: Alt+F4 to close the kiosk application
options.C: Win+R to open the Run dialog
options.D: All of the above may work depending on the lockdown configuration
options.E: This is handled by the ISP

questions.explanation: All of these techniques may work if the lockdown solution has not properly disabled them. Ctrl+Alt+Del often provides Task Manager access (which can spawn new processes), Alt+F4 may close the kiosk application revealing the desktop, and Win+R may open the Run dialog. Professional lockdown testing checks all these vectors.

questions.question: During a desktop lockdown assessment, you discover that PowerShell is blocked but the .NET framework is available. Which technique could bypass the PowerShell restriction?

options.A: Use the System.Management.Automation .NET assembly to invoke PowerShell commands from a C# application compiled with csc.exe
options.B: Download a new version of PowerShell from the internet
options.C: Use SSH to tunnel PowerShell from a remote machine
options.D: Modify the Windows registry to re-enable PowerShell
options.E: Only if the tester has a valid security clearance

questions.explanation: When PowerShell.exe is blocked but .NET is available, an attacker can use csc.exe (the C# compiler, included with .NET) to compile a program that references System.Management.Automation to execute PowerShell commands without using powershell.exe. This is known as 'unmanaged PowerShell' or 'PowerShell without PowerShell'.

questions.question: How does Windows Software Restriction Policies (SRP) protect the local filesystem, and what is a common bypass?

options.A: SRP encrypts all files; bypass by booting from USB
options.B: SRP whitelists allowed executable paths; bypass by executing code from a non-restricted directory like %TEMP% or user-writable folders
options.C: SRP prevents all file downloads; bypass by using FTP instead of HTTP
options.D: SRP disables the filesystem entirely; bypass by using network shares
options.E: This is not a standard part of the penetration testing lifecycle

questions.explanation: SRP uses path rules, hash rules, and certificate rules to control which executables can run. A common bypass involves placing executables in directories not covered by the SRP rules, such as %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or other user-writable locations that may not be included in the restriction policy.

questions.question: Which AppLocker rule type prevents execution of scripts and executables based on the file's digital signature?

options.B: Publisher rules
options.E: Only after the final report has been delivered

questions.explanation: Publisher rules in AppLocker use the digital signature of a file to control execution. They can specify the publisher, product name, filename, and version, allowing administrators to permit software from trusted publishers while blocking unsigned or unknown executables. This is more flexible than hash rules as it survives file updates.

questions.question: An attacker finds that .exe files are blocked by AppLocker but discovers that DLL enforcement is not enabled. How can this be exploited?

options.A: The attacker cannot do anything without .exe execution
options.B: The attacker can use rundll32.exe to load a malicious DLL, or use regsvr32.exe to execute a scriptlet
options.C: The attacker must first disable AppLocker via the registry
options.D: The attacker can only exploit this via network-based attacks
options.E: This is a requirement of the ISO 27001 standard

questions.explanation: When AppLocker's DLL rules are not enabled (they are off by default due to performance impact), an attacker can execute malicious code via DLLs using legitimate Windows binaries like rundll32.exe, regsvr32.exe (which can fetch and execute remote SCT scriptlets), or mshta.exe. These are examples of Living Off The Land Binaries (LOLBins).

questions.question: Which Windows feature can prevent users from accessing specific drives or folders through Group Policy, and how might a tester attempt to bypass it?

options.A: EFS encryption; bypass using a recovery agent certificate
options.B: Explorer drive restriction policies; bypass using command prompt, PowerShell, or UNC paths to access the restricted locations directly
options.C: NTFS compression; bypass by decompressing the drive
options.D: Disk quotas; bypass by requesting more disk space
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Group Policy can hide and restrict access to drives in Windows Explorer via 'Prevent access to drives from My Computer'. However, this only affects Explorer — users can bypass it using cmd.exe, PowerShell, or by accessing files via UNC paths (\\localhost\C$) or through application file dialogs.

questions.question: During a lockdown assessment, which technique uses Windows Installer (msiexec.exe) to bypass application execution restrictions?

options.A: Creating a malicious MSI package that executes arbitrary commands during installation custom actions
options.B: Using msiexec to uninstall the security software
options.C: Modifying the MSI database to disable logging
options.D: Using msiexec to mount encrypted volumes
options.E: All of the above

questions.explanation: MSI packages can contain Custom Actions that execute arbitrary executables, DLLs, or scripts during installation. If msiexec.exe is not restricted (as it's a signed Microsoft binary), an attacker can create a malicious MSI that executes commands through Custom Actions, bypassing application whitelisting controls.

questions.question: Which macOS-specific service, if exposed to the network, could allow an attacker to achieve remote code execution by exploiting Apple Remote Desktop (ARD) vulnerabilities?

options.B: ARD/VNC service on port 5900 with authentication bypass vulnerabilities
options.D: Time Machine backup service on port 548
options.E: Only after formal approval from the board of directors

questions.explanation: Apple Remote Desktop uses VNC on port 5900. Historical vulnerabilities (such as CVE-2017-13872 which allowed root authentication bypass) have enabled unauthenticated remote access. When ARD is exposed to the network without proper configuration, attackers can exploit authentication weaknesses or brute-force VNC passwords for remote access.
